key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, achieving a roughly €3.53 million net present cost with fewer simulations than tested black-box baselines.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce simulation costs when sizing integrated energy technologies, including photovoltaics, batteries and heat pumps; it does not optimize solar cells themselves.
method: Propose configuration changes using prior simulation results and structured memory.
Evaluate designs with year-long simulations and a 25-year net present cost objective.
Use constrained actions and git-based keep/revert decisions to retain improvements and audit decisions.
evidence_signal: On one measured-load building case, LLM agents received 50 simulations per run versus 300 for baselines; Opus reached the best design in all ten runs and came within 1% after a median of 18 simulations.
watch_item: Results come from a single building case, and reliability varied across models, so broader validation is needed before generalizing performance.
paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
